title: The Brain Has No Center
excerpt: We keep looking for the little witness inside the skull. The stranger possibility is that a self can be real without having a single place where it lives.
content:
There is a moment in every explanation of the brain when I want to ask: yes, but where am I? Not which region is active, not which network is communicating, but where is the person to whom all this is happening?

The honest answer is slightly disappointing. There is no small room behind the forehead where a witness watches the screens. Experience is spread across systems that remember, predict, sort, and revise. The feeling of being one person is something they manage together.

That does not make the feeling fake. A city has no single building where the city lives. It can still wake, grieve, celebrate, and change. Perhaps the self is like that: not an object hidden somewhere, but a pattern that becomes visible in the way many ordinary things hold together.

I find this less frightening when I stop treating unity as a possession. I do not need to locate the self like a coin under a cushion. I only need to notice the work by which, for a little while, a life feels like mine.
